key_insight: InFlux++ extends the study of dynamic camera intrinsics by combining real-world and synthetic data to better estimate frame-by-frame camera parameters from RGB video. This helps 3D vision systems handle videos where camera zoom, focus, or other intrinsics change over time.
problem_solved: Most 3D reconstruction and video understanding methods assume camera intrinsics stay fixed across a video, which is often false in real-world footage. This paper addresses the challenge of estimating per-frame intrinsics for videos with dynamic camera settings.
method: Uses both real and synthetic data to train and evaluate dynamic intrinsic estimation.
Builds on the InFlux benchmark, which provides real-world per-frame ground-truth intrinsics for dynamic videos.
Focuses on predicting camera intrinsics directly from RGB frames to support downstream 3D methods.
impact: This matters for practitioners because more accurate intrinsics estimation can make 3D reconstruction, SLAM, and video-based geometry methods robust to in-the-wild videos. It reduces failure cases caused by the common but unrealistic assumption of fixed intrinsics.

paper_title: InFlux++: Real and Synthetic Data for Estimating Dynamic Camera Intrinsics
